contract: Provider-neutral batch job mode over integration/ai-text requests: submit 1..max_items {item_id, text_request} (item ids ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$, unique; one model; each item admitted exactly as the synchronous text admission; count, payload, item and exact provider create-body bytes bounded) as a core/effect declaration with local refusals before any intent; submit and cancel are writes through delivery/effect-intent bindings; the provider create body is prepared once at admission and the submit intent arguments are a manifest naming it (count, length, SHA-256, non-secret provider metadata); the host stages the body in a store capability {module, pid or registered name} (no function accepted) and the Adapter sends exactly the fetched bytes after checking them against the manifest; outcomes submitted{job_ref, item_count, orphans} | refused{reason, retry_after, orphans} | unknown{reason, orphans} and cancelled{job_state} | refused | unknown, using ELZ-079's Cure failure table (only credentials_unavailable attested no-send; a lost submit or cancel stays unknown and a second dispatch of the same identity is refused); status and bounded result pages are call-scoped reads; results are joined by item id, unknown or duplicate ids refuse the page, missing ids are reported only after the last page of an ended job; item completions get the synchronous completion checks; conformance kit.
limits: The result sink is volatile local delivery: an owner restart between the provider's answer and the sink call loses the job reference; the caller owns its durability and the polling cadence.

A missing or substituted staged body sends nothing but is reported unknown (provider_error), because the reused failure table attests no-send only for credentials; after a host restart the staged body is gone unless the host persisted it.
No reconciliation of a lost submit or cancel is offered: no provider in this slice returns a caller tag or a cancel receipt; a status observation is not a ground.
Result pages re-read the provider's result stream from the start when the provider has no paging; under a scan bound smaller than the result file a deep cursor returns result_scan_limit.
Completion-check equality with the synchronous text path is shown over a named finite corpus only; SHA-256 collision resistance is an upstream assumption.

No poll scheduling, webhooks, embeddings or other endpoints in batch, cost or price computation, or result retention beyond the provider's window; finite scenarios with scripted providers and a volatile store; no proof is claimed.

grounding.claim: Both batch bindings compile ELZ-079's static failure table of the pinned Cure decision Elzoo.AiTextOutcome; configure/1 refuses construction unless the table equals the Cure decision at run time. Not a proof of provider behaviour.

Listed scenarios with scripted providers and the volatile Memory store: submit accepted through the owner with manifest arguments, the provider receiving bytes identical to the body the admission digest names, and no staged bytes, prompt or credential in the owner state's external term format; function and non-pid lookup capabilities refused at configuration; substituted bodies (changed byte, another admission's body) send nothing; local refusals before intent, credential and provider (duplicate and malformed ids, mixed models, counts, bytes at bound - 1, bound, bound + 1 and wrapper overhead, invalid items, undeclared features and options); configuration bounds; orphans on every outcome; lost submit unknown and second dispatch refused; credential failure the only no-send; missing or mismatched staged submission sends nothing; cancel acknowledged, lost and refused with the second dispatch refused; every job state; results joined by item id out of order, unknown and duplicate ids within and across pages refused, missing ids after the last page only, page, line and scan bounds; per-item usage unknown and malformed items; completion equality with the synchronous ai-text path over a named corpus; redaction in deliveries, errors, inspect and logs; a source audit of this Piece's own listed files. Finite scenarios, not proofs.
OTP 29.1.2 crypto SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA-256; SHA-256 collision resistance is assumed, not proved.
Relies on pinned compilation of the reused ELZ-079 outcome decision; not a local proof of the compiler.
jsv 0.27.0 schema build and validation through the text interface's Schema module for tool proposals and structured output, as exercised in the listed scenarios.

Batch provider Pieces implement the behaviour truthfully (one request per operation, documented statuses, absent usage fields :unknown, orphans reported); the host's submission lookup returns only the bytes it staged for that intent, binding and manifest; the credential Need is truthful.

telemetry.contract: No Elzoo event. Own events through runtime/telemetry: future task when a consumer needs them. Not inherited: runtime/telemetry is not a dependency.

config.contract: Construction-time submit and cancel bindings (provider account in the intent key), tenant, provider and its term, credential Need, submission lookup Need, model allowlist, per-item output cap, max_items and max_create_wire_bytes within the provider's caps, payload and item byte bounds, page size, result line and scan byte bounds, receive timeout and result sink; deadlines from the declarations; no hot reconfiguration.

control.contract: Call-scoped reads; dispatch, rearm and expiry of submit and cancel are the delivery/effect-intent owner's Control; cancel is a request to the provider, not a local drain.
